name: MemberArea API
description:
The MemberArea API exposes your MemberArea: members, courses, hubs, events,
products, orders and the community, as a clean REST interface. All endpoints
are scoped to the MemberArea that owns the API key.

**Base URL:** `https://api.memberarea.io/v1`

**Authentication:** Two credentials open the same API.

- **API key**, the MemberArea's own credential, created by its owner under
  Settings → API keys. Send it as `X-Api-Key: mak_…` (preferred) or
  `Authorization: Bearer mak_…`. Right for your own scripts and for an
  integration that serves one MemberArea.
- **OAuth 2.0 access token**, for software that other MemberAreas connect.
  An administrator approves your application on a consent screen and you
  receive a token you send as `Authorization: Bearer mao_…`. Nobody pastes
  a key into your product, the grant covers only the scopes you asked for,
  and it can be withdrawn at any time. The **OAuth** section below walks
  the whole flow.

**Scopes:** Every key carries an explicit list of scopes; each endpoint
names the one it needs. Where two are listed, either will do. The
`wordpress:read` scope is meant for a key you hand to a website you connect:
it opens only what such a site displays, and it narrows the answers, so
drafts, hidden entries and your own contact details stay out of reach.
A few endpoints are not key-authenticated at all and say so.

**Envelope:** Successful responses use `{ "data": ..., "meta": ... }`. Every
error carries `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": ... } }`,
including the ones raised before an endpoint runs (missing key, missing
scope, rate limit) and every validation failure. Switch on `error.code`
alone; you never need a second shape.

Errors raised outside an endpoint additionally keep the framework's own
keys next to the envelope: `message`, plus `errors` with one array of
messages per rejected field on a validation failure. Those keys are kept
for clients written before the envelope was universal; `error.message`
repeats `message` and `error.details` repeats `errors`, so nothing is lost
by reading the envelope only. Errors raised inside an endpoint carry the
envelope alone.

Most codes are specific to the endpoint and named in its description. The
ones that can appear anywhere, derived from the status when nothing more
precise applies, are: `bad_request`, `unauthenticated`, `payment_required`,
`forbidden`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_acceptable`,
`conflict`, `gone`, `payload_too_large`, `unsupported_media_type`,
`validation_failed`, `locked`, `rate_limited`, `not_implemented`,
`service_unavailable` and `server_error`. An unrecognised code should be
treated by its HTTP status.

One documented exception: the automation webhook answers with a bare
`{ "error": "<code>" }` string. It is a receiver, not an endpoint you call,
and its shape is frozen so existing senders keep working. That endpoint is
excluded from the envelope entirely, including its framework-level errors.

**Pagination:** List endpoints return up to 25 items by default. Pass
`?per_page=50` (max 100) and `?page=N` to control pagination. `meta`
contains `page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`.

**IDs:** Resources are addressed by their `id` field, an opaque string.
Treat it as a token: don't parse or construct it.

**Rate limits:** Requests are metered per API key in staggered buckets:
600 reads/min, 120 writes/min, and 30 automation triggers/min, plus daily
caps on top. Exceeding a bucket returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header
and `X-RateLimit-*` headers describing the limit, the remaining budget and
the reset time.

**Plan limits:** Write actions that would cross a plan boundary (for
example creating members beyond `limit_members`) are rejected with `402`
and `{ "error": { "code": "plan_limit_reached", ... } }`.
